fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Circular Driveway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the opening for large emergency vehicles.
• Keep the full width of the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and landscaping to allow two-way movement for emergency vehicles.
• Maintain the circular driveway free of obstacles so arriving units can pull forward and turn around without backing out onto the road.
• Identify and mark any alternate rear access point across the open terrain so responders are not limited to the single front driveway.
• Keep any perimeter fence gates accessible and unlocked, or provide a lock box with a standardized key, so responders can reach the rear of the property without delay.
• Post the property address on the residence itself in numbers visible from the driveway approach.
• Designate a clear staging area on the circular driveway or adjacent open space where command and support vehicles can park without blocking the access drive.
• Trim any landscaping along the access drive that narrows the usable width or reduces sight lines for approaching vehicles.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Brush Area; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the structure.
• Remove dead or dry grass from within a few feet of the structure's base.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopy and the building.
• Clear brush from the edges of the driveway to keep the single access route open for vehicles.
• Keep overhanging tree branches trimmed back from above the driveway.
• Remove dense brush patches closest to the structure before dry season.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation in the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Separate shrub groupings near any outbuildings or fences connected to the main structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches and overgrown vegetation along its full length.
• Cut back shrubs along the driveway entry point to maintain clear sightlines for entering and exiting vehicles.
